Key Research Thinking Patterns: Empirical Measurement and Systematic Quantification: Rigorously measures and quantifies complex, often intangible, phenomena to create concrete baselines and models (e.g., deploys honeypots to measure the specific volume and type of reconnaissance attacks against P2P nodes, quantifying the threat level differences between standard servers and Ethereum nodes).

Longitudinal and Temporal Analysis: Focuses on how systems, threats, and behaviors evolve over time to understand their dynamics and persistence (e.g., creates the multi-year MagnetDB dataset (2018-2024) to analyze long-term supply-side trends in digital piracy and formally defines "Temporal Investment" as a core construct in dataset valuation).

Data Curation and Enrichment as Core Research Act: Treats the creation, annotation, and enrichment of datasets as a primary research contribution, not just a preliminary step (e.g., develops the MagnetDB dataset by not only collecting torrents but also enriching them by matching files to the IMDb database, enabling deeper supply-side analysis).

Sociotechnical and Ethical/Governance Analysis: Investigates the human, social, and systemic context of technology, including its ethical implications and governance needs (e.g., analyzes the subcultural "gift economy" of "The Scene" to explain the supply-side dynamics of digital piracy and proposes a formal taxonomy (DVT) to guide the ethical governance and funding of data assets).
Summary Description: Dr. Anindya Maiti specializes in cybersecurity and data-centric AI, investigating the interplay between system vulnerabilities, generative AI, and human-computer interaction. His research empirically quantifies security threats in decentralized P2P networks, such as reconnaissance attacks on Ethereum nodes, and in AI-native systems, including package hallucinations in code-generating LLMs. He also analyzes human-AI collaboration, studying the efficacy of iterative prompt refinement for image regeneration. A central theme is data curation as a core scholarly contribution, demonstrated by his creation of MagnetDB, a large-scale longitudinal dataset for studying digital piracy, and his development of the Dataset Value Taxonomy (DVT) to formally assess dataset value in empirical research.
